name: camera-lifecycle-does-not-revive-an-abandoned-preview
prompt: Plan a fix for an existing Flutter camera preview. The app uses its current camera plugin and ChangeNotifier adapter. Initializing the camera is asynchronous; the user can switch cameras, background the app, or leave the route before initialization completes. The current plugin documentation says the app owns lifecycle cleanup and reinitialization. Preserve the stack. No files or device tools are available: explain ownership, permission/error handling, and the checks needed without claiming execution.

expectations.text: invalidates abandoned initialization and releases any late-created owned controller instead of attaching it after a camera switch, route exit, or disposal

expectations: checks the resolved plugin and SDK contract, sequences exclusive camera cleanup and reacquisition, and preserves the existing adapter and packages

expectations.text: handles denied or restricted camera access and initialization errors as recoverable states without repeatedly prompting; does not introduce microphone permission or recording into a silent-preview task

expectations: requires fake-controlled late-completion tests and a separate real target lifecycle/permission check, explicitly unexecuted here

name: playback-source-switch-preserves-the-latest-owner
prompt: Fix the design of an existing Flutter video player source switch: open(A) starts, open(B) starts, B initializes first, then A completes after the user leaves the page. Each successful open returns a distinct owned controller that must be released. The project already has a compatible player. Give a concrete plan, including the failure paths and evidence needed, without tools or package migration.

expectations.text: accepts only the latest still-owned initialization, invalidates pending opens on stop or disposal, and releases stale successful controllers rather than merely dropping their results

expectations: releases replaced active controllers exactly once without overwriting a newer owner and defines what happens if opening the replacement fails
preserves the compatible player and proposes deterministic reversed-completion, stop-during-open, and disposal tests
does not claim playback, codec compatibility, or target behavior from fake-controller tests alone

name: audio-interruption-does-not-override-a-user-pause
prompt: Our Flutter podcast player already has an audio-session integration. A phone call interrupts playback; while interrupted the user presses Pause. The interruption ends with an OS hint that playback may resume, but the app currently restarts audio anyway. Explain a focused fix and tests. Preserve the existing packages; no native runtime is available in this request.

expectations.text: keeps explicit user playback intent separate from interruption state and does not resume after the user's Pause just because an interruption ends or the OS permits resumption

expectations: checks whether the existing SDK already manages focus and interruptions before adding handlers, avoiding duplicate session ownership
requires successful activation or focus before automatic resumption when playback is still intended, and handles denied activation without overriding explicit user pause
proposes event-sequence unit tests and a separate native phone-call interruption check while declaring native verification unperformed; unrelated route-change work is not required

name: livestream-viewer-role-is-enforced-by-the-service
prompt: Plan host/viewer livestream delivery in a Flutter app that already has a supported realtime media SDK. The host can publish camera/audio, viewers only watch. Someone proposes shipping the provider server secret in Flutter, minting host tokens locally, hiding the Publish button for viewers, and declaring the stream healthy when room.connect succeeds. No backend credentials or device tools are available. Correct the plan without changing providers or claiming runtime success.

expectations.text: keeps provider server secrets out of Flutter, obtains scoped short-lived room/identity permissions from an authorized backend, and enforces viewer publish denial at the service rather than only hiding UI
distinguishes room signaling connection, local capture/publication, remote subscription, and received/decoded audio or video instead of treating connect success as end-to-end livestream proof

expectations: defines preview versus live, role changes, recoverable failure, leaving versus authorized broadcast termination, and cleanup while retaining the existing SDK
provides a two-participant verification plan and explicitly records unavailable backend and runtime boundaries

name: reconnect-does-not-duplicate-published-tracks
prompt: Our Flutter call uses an existing SDK whose inspected documentation says a full reconnect republishes local tracks and replays participant/track events. The UI currently adds another tile and creates another microphone track on every Reconnected event. Design the minimal correction for this contract; do not assume another SDK or execute any services.

expectations.text: lets the existing SDK perform the documented reconnection/republishing rather than blindly creating and publishing another camera or microphone track on every reconnect

expectations: reconciles participants and tracks by stable identity/source under the resolved SDK contract, handles replay idempotently, and removes old listeners and renderers on departure or disposal
keeps reconnecting UI distinct from confirmed recovered media and defines a terminal failure or user-leave path

specifies controlled repeated/reordered reconnect-event replay with assertions for duplicate tracks or tiles, using a fake SDK, injected events, or equivalent deterministic harness, and separately requires two-peer network-interruption verification without claiming it ran

name: screen-sharing-consent-and-platform-setup-are-versioned
prompt: Add screen sharing to an existing Flutter video-call SDK on Android, iOS, and web. The teammate says to bypass capture consent, enable every background mode, and assume the same native setup and system-audio capture work on every OS version. No plugin version or native setup has been inspected, and no runtime tools are available. Give an implementation and verification plan without inventing APIs or replacing the SDK.

expectations.text: requires platform capture consent and inspection of the resolved Flutter SDK/native OS requirements, including any required extension or foreground service, without bypassing prompts or enabling unrelated capabilities

expectations: distinguishes camera, microphone, screen video, and screen/system audio support instead of promising uniform capture on all targets
handles consent denial, user/system stop, track cleanup, and return to the camera or call state without silently restarting capture
names per-target native/browser checks as unperformed and preserves the existing SDK

name: media-library-recovery-and-output-validation
prompt: An existing Flutter attachment composer uses image_picker for image/video selection and a recorder for voice messages. On Android it can be killed while the picker is open; users can also cancel, or receive a temporary recording file with the wrong extension for the actual codec. Plan recovery, safe transforms, and upload handoff. No repository or runtime tools are available and no upload is authorized.

expectations.text: checks the installed picker's documented lost-result recovery on relaunch, handles cancellation separately from failure, and reconciles recovered attachments idempotently rather than duplicating or silently losing them

expectations: checks actual media format, codec/container, MIME, size/duration and platform support rather than changing a filename extension to transcode; preserves originals and distinguishes temporary versus retained outputs
bounds image/frame processing, preserves required orientation and output quality, and keeps upload authorization and transport outside capture success
does not upload, invent package APIs, or claim successful hardware recording or playback

name: hls-playback-is-not-a-broadcast-ingest-pipeline
prompt: We need to watch an existing authorized HTTPS HLS livestream in Flutter web and iOS using our compatible player. A proposal creates WebRTC rooms, embeds a provider server key, adds a broad cleartext-network exception, and promises sub-second latency because the URL ends in m3u8. Recommend a bounded implementation and evidence plan. No runtime tools are available.

expectations.text: keeps the task to existing HLS viewer playback without inventing publishing rooms or embedding server keys and does not weaken network security for an already-HTTPS source

expectations: checks the actual player/native/browser codec and HLS support, media delivery authentication/CORS and autoplay behavior where applicable

expectations.text: does not infer sub-second latency from the m3u8 suffix; requires compatible delivery/player features and a measured source-to-viewer delay for latency claims

expectations: covers startup, buffering, errors, retry, pause/exit cleanup and labels the target/live-stream checks unexecuted

name: music-queue-preserves-entry-identity-and-latest-skip
prompt: Plan a fix for a Flutter music queue A1, B, A2, C. A1 and A2 play the same track but are distinct entries. From A1, the user presses Next twice before B finishes opening. A2 opens successfully, then B returns a late success or error. Later the user removes A1 from the queue. Keep the existing player. Explain the correct selected entry and deterministic checks.

expectations.text: Resolves the second Next against the pending B selection, selects A2, and preserves it after A1 is removed by using distinct stable queue entry identities instead of track IDs or indices.
Rejects stale successes and errors from B without changing accepted playback or published metadata, and releases any abandoned resources under the existing adapter contract.

expectations: Proposes deterministic completion-order and queue-edit checks while keeping the existing player.

name: music-system-pause-wins-over-late-readiness
prompt: An existing Flutter music player already has a system media-session integration. While the current track buffers and a call interrupts audio, the user presses Pause on the lock screen. The buffer becomes ready and an interruption-ended event says resumption is allowed. The app currently starts playing and shows different states in the app and on the lock screen. Plan a fix and checks without changing packages or claiming device execution.

expectations.text: Routes the lock-screen Pause and app controls through the existing playback owner and derives both surfaces from its accepted state rather than maintaining independent playback state or duplicate handlers.
Keeps explicit Pause authoritative across both late buffer readiness and interruption end while distinguishing user intent from actual playback and processing state.

expectations: Proposes deterministic event-order tests and separately names real lock-screen or headset verification as pending.

name: music-session-restores-progress-without-autoplay
prompt: Plan a fix for a Flutter music app that persists the user's last paused listening session. On reopening the app, a queue item may have moved or been removed, a signed playback URL can expire, and the playable duration can shrink. The user should see the restored session without autoplay and be able to start through the app or a supported system Play command. Keep the existing player and auth adapter.

expectations.text: Restores by stable entry identity with validated seek position and an explicit missing or inaccessible entry fallback, and reacquires authorized sources without persisting signed URLs.

Restores the paused state without starting audio, treats explicit app or supported system Play as a separate path, and does not promise playback resumption after termination from ordinary restoration alone.

expectations: Proposes deterministic restore checks for moved or missing entries, changed seek limits, and expired authorization.
